scope: The four confirmed interface findings and necessary current UI ownership/recovery dependencies. No realtime implementation or tests were edited.
method: Diagnosed the existing failing cleanup test first with temporary local trace instrumentation, then restored the test and implemented snapshot-bound confirmation. Updated the four assigned UI components and the shared workflow/recovery controls. Bound asynchronous effects to stable per-scope owner tokens, explicit operation identities and input draft generations; retained original global operation reconciliation and unknown-outcome blocks. Added regression cases for text/ref/scope ABA transitions, same-revision different worktree identities, late accepted and failed responses, retained drafts, directory pagination/refresh and both cross-scope and same-scope recovery queries. Ran only explicit affected test files through scripts/run-tests.mjs --targeted and Web TypeScript checks. No full suite, SSH, online instance changes, real shell execution, external MCP or personal configuration was used. Earlier frozen-source component artifacts in .work were used solely to verify the exact prior TerminalRow state transition from this same task; no older repository or historical implementation was consulted.

resolvedFindings.change: Import attempts capture a stable owner, input text revision and attempt identity. A late file result cannot overwrite any intervening edit, including A-to-B-to-A. The UI reports that the current draft was retained. Failed reads preserve text, scope ABA cannot revive the old import, and skill confirmation is bound to the current owner.

Create and existing-worktree action forms are mutually exclusive. Confirmation carries owner, action, worktreeId, live phase and revision, or the exact creation ref. Selection and ref changes explicitly clear it. Epoch/connection ownership changes invalidate it synchronously. Late creation responses cannot close a newer scope form.

A command acknowledgement clears only the exact captured draft object, not an equal text value. Command or timeout edits advance the draft generation; errors retain the draft. Consent and status belong to a stable owner. Shared workflow ownership prevents prior thread/epoch/connection outcomes from changing a newer UI owner while Api still records and acknowledges the actual global outcome.

Event subscription consent is bound to API/session/epoch/thread/server/connection ownership, invalidated by every parameter edit and consumed at submission. Server/scope ABA never restores consent. Pending results and failures preserve edited parameters, and an old service acknowledgement does not clear a new service draft or its independently supplied confirmation.

additionalFindings.trigger: Confirm cleanup before loading all background-terminal pages, then load another page.
additionalFindings.impact: The old boolean confirmation remained checked after the second page rendered and the cleanup button became enabled before the effect cleared it. The existing test clicked this still-checked checkbox again, cancelling consent, so no cleanup was sent. This was a real transient confirmation boundary defect, not a reason to weaken the test.
additionalFindings.resolution: Confirmation is derived synchronously from owner, resource key and exact items snapshot. It is disabled until the complete directory is ready and invalidated by refresh/pagination/scope changes. The existing cleanup intent and accepted-result assertions are preserved and now pass.

additionalFindings.trigger: A later page replaces an already confirmed terminal row with a new object carrying the same processId and displayed fields.
additionalFindings.impact: The JSON-based React key retained the old boolean confirmation and allowed termination against the refreshed row without fresh confirmation.
additionalFindings.resolution: Each terminal confirmation is tied to the exact row object and stable scope. The new pagination replacement regression requires it to reset. Existing command/identity-change protection via row validation and keys is retained.

additionalFindings.trigger: An operation/read query completes after its UI scope changes, or after another operation becomes the current recovery target in the same scope.
additionalFindings.impact: The old query called action.refresh() on the replacement owner. In the concrete worktree regression, an old creation receipt dismissed the newer unknown archive intent.
additionalFindings.resolution: useWorkflow exports a stable owner token and current-owner predicate. ExtensionStatus additionally captures operationId, scopes busy/error state and guards refresh and callbacks. Valid original receipts still reconcile globally; stale UI errors and refreshes are dropped. Both accepted and failed late query cases and same-scope operation replacement are covered.
